podcast.body: Released in 1994, this song sounded notably similar to Wire's 1977 track "Three Girl Rumba." Elastica's leader, Justine Frieshmund, admitted to deliberately "nicking" elements of Wire's song, leading to a settlement where Elastica surrendered a portion of their first album's royalties to Wire. "Elastica with connection from 1994, which sounded awfully similar to Three Girl Rumbaw from Wire, which was recorded in 1977."

podcast.body: This 1994 song "sounds awfully familiar" to Wire's "Three Girl Rumba" from 1977. Justine Frischmann, Elastica's leader and a "huge Wire fan," openly "admitted to being such a big fan that she deliberately nicks some of Three Girl Rumba for one of her songs." This admission of guilt led to Elastica surrendering "a certain amount of the royalties from that first album to Wire." "Elastica with connection from 1994, which sounds awfully familiar to Three Girl Rumba from Wire from 1977."

podcast.body: This song from Elastica's debut album was notably similar to Wire's 1977 track "Three Girl Rumba." Elastica's leader, Justine Frischmann, admitted to being a "huge Wire fan" and deliberately taking elements from their song as a tribute, leading to a ruling that Elastica surrender a portion of the album's royalties to Wire. "The Elastica with connection from 1994, which sounds awfully familiar to Three Girl Rumba from Wire from 1977."
